blocks.text: JavaScript Number Methods

rows:
Basic Methods
Basic number methods can be used on any number:
toString()
toExponential()
toFixed()
toPrecision()
valueOf()

Static Methods
Static methods can only be used on Number:
Number.isFinite()
Number.isInteger()
Number.isNan()
Number.isSafeInteger()
Number.parseInt()
Number.parseFloat()

The toString() Method
The toString() method returns a number as a string.
All number methods can be used on any type of numbers (literals, variables, or expressions):

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text:
The toString() method can take an optional radix argument to convert
the number to a different base:

let x = 123;

let text = x.toString(2);
blocks.caption: Example

A parameter defines the number of characters behind the decimal point:

blocks.text: The valueOf() Method
valueOf() returns a number as a number.

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text:
In JavaScript, a number can be a primitive value (typeof = number) or an
object (typeof = object).

The valueOf() method is used internally in JavaScript to convert Number
objects to primitive values.
There is no reason to use it in your code.
All JavaScript data types have a valueOf() and a toString() method.
Converting Variables to Numbers

There are 3 JavaScript methods that can be used
to convert a variable to a number:

rows: Number()
Returns a number converted from its argument.
parseFloat()
Parses its argument and returns a floating point number
parseInt()
Parses its argument and returns a whole number

blocks.text: The methods above are not number methods. They are global JavaScript methods.
The Number() Method
The Number() method can be used to convert JavaScript variables to numbers:

blocks.text: If the number cannot be converted, NaN (Not a Number) is returned.
The Number() Method Used on Dates
Number() can also convert a date to a number.
Number(new Date("1970-01-01"))
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The Date() method returns the number of milliseconds since 1.1.1970.
The number of milliseconds between 1970-01-02 and 1970-01-01 is 86400000:
Number(new Date("1970-01-02"))
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: Number(new Date("2017-09-30"))

Number Object Methods
These object methods belong to the Number object:

rows: Number.isInteger()
Returns true if the argument is an integer
Number.isNaN()
Returns true if the argument is NaN
Number.isFinite()
Returns true if the argument is not Infinity nor NaN
Number.isSafeInteger()
Returns true if the argument is a safe integer
Number.parseFloat()
Converts a string to a number
Number.parseInt()
Converts a string to a whole number

blocks.text: Number Methods Cannot be Used on Variables
The number methods above belong to the JavaScript Number Object.
These methods can only be accessed like Number.isInteger().
Using X.isInteger() where X is a variable, will result in an error:
TypeError X.isInteger is not a function.
The Number.isInteger() Method
The Number.isInteger() method returns true if the argument is an integer.

Number.isInteger(10);

Number.isInteger(10.5);
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The Number.isFinite() Method

The Number.isFinite() method returns true
if the argument is not Infinity, -iInfinity, nor Nan.
Number.isFinite(123);
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The Number.isNaN() Method

The Number.isNaN() method returns true
if the argument is NaN (Not a Number).
Number.isNaN(123);
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text:
Number.isNaN() is the preferred way to check for equality with NaN.
You cannot test for equality with NaN using == or ===.
The Number.isSafeInteger() Method
A safe integer is an integer that can be exactly represented as a double precision number.
The Number.isSafeInteger() method returns true if the argument is a safe integer.

Number.isSafeInteger(10);

Number.isSafeInteger(12345678901234567890);
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The Number.parseFloat() Method
Number.parseFloat() parses a string and returns a number.
Spaces are allowed. Only the first number is returned:

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: If the number cannot be converted, NaN (Not a Number) is returned.

The Number methods Number.parseInt()
and Number.parseFloat()
are the same as the
Global methods parseInt() and parseFloat().

The purpose of these two methods is modularization of globals, to make it easier to use the same
JavaScript code outside the browser.
The Number.parseInt() Method
Number.parseInt() parses a string and returns a whole number.

The Number.isInteger() method returns true if the argument is an integer.

blocks.text: The Number.isSafeInteger() Method
A safe integer is an integer that can be exactly represented as a double precision number.
The Number.isSafeInteger() method returns true if the argument is a safe integer.

Number.isSafeInteger(10);

Number.isSafeInteger(12345678901234567890);
blocks.caption: Example isSafeInteger()

blocks.text:
Safe integers are all integers from -(253 - 1) to +(253 - 1).
This is safe: 9007199254740991. This is not safe: 9007199254740992.
